title: Choose Cocktail Grimoire’s visual world
question: Choose the world that should carry a growing collection of 20–30+ recipes. Every option keeps the same YAML-only content and dynamic glassware SVG system.

options.label: The Chromatic Glass Cabinet
options.lineage: museum glass study cabinets and illuminated specimen cases
options.thesis: Every recipe is a numbered glass specimen, with its YAML accent behaving like light through the drink.
options.viewport: A restrained masthead gives most of the screen to a dense cabinet grid of large glass silhouettes, recipe numbers, and names; opening one expands that same specimen into the detail composition.
options.risk: It fails if the cabinet becomes a conventional card grid or the glass drawings are treated as small icons.

raised.raise: Every cocktail receives a recognizable silhouette and repeatable personal identity, not merely a color swap.
The specimen field preserves a strong measured scale as metadata rearranges around it on smaller screens.
The index-to-detail transition treats the SVG specimen as continuous material across routes.
The collection reflows in whole cabinet bays so twenty or thirty recipes still read as one ordered installation.

options.label: The Spirit Label Proof Archive
options.lineage: distillery label proofs, overprint swatches, and printer’s registration sheets
options.thesis: The collection is an archive of numbered label proofs, each cocktail authored in its own accent ink.
options.viewport: A compact archive header sits above a scalable proof-sheet grid where each large cocktail logo, number, and factual metadata lock to visible registration furniture.
options.risk: Label and editorial systems are a familiar destination for drinks brands, so craft must prevent it from feeling expected.

options.label: The Cocktail Plate Annual
options.lineage: design annual plate sections on uncoated stock
options.thesis: Each recipe is a generous editorial plate inside one continuous, carefully registered collection sheet.
options.viewport: An oversized collection title and one hero plate establish the book, followed immediately by a precise multi-column index that can grow without changing its grammar.
options.case: It matches the modern-book identity and gives metadata exceptional clarity; it is less immediately cocktail-specific than the glass cabinet.
options.risk: Its refinement can become anonymous portfolio minimalism if the cocktail illustrations do not dominate each plate.

options.label: The Cocktail Assembly Book
options.thesis: A cocktail becomes a measured assembly: ingredients, glass, and garnish lock together with diagrammatic certainty.
options.viewport: The index presents completed glass assemblies in a strict modular roster; each detail route reorganizes the same SVG into an ingredient-and-glass instruction spread.
options.case: It makes recipes exceptionally legible and gives SVGs a native job; its toy-world associations identify less naturally with a modern cocktail book.
options.risk: The language can become juvenile unless linework, type, and motion stay exact and restrained.

options.label: The Cocktail Character Roster
options.thesis: Every glass illustration behaves like a distinct cast member in a growing roster.
options.viewport: A ranked-looking roster of large glass personalities introduces the collection as a cast.
options.case: The identity system scales, but ranking and mascot behavior conflict with an unfiltered personal recipe book.
options.kept: Distinct silhouette and personality must survive even when accent colors are similar.
options.risk: It turns a mature mixing reference into character merchandise.

options.label: The Flavor Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscopes and measured signal benches
options.thesis: Profiles and measures become traces surrounding a locked glass silhouette.
options.viewport: One active recipe occupies a measured screen while the broader collection behaves like selectable channels.
options.case: Its measurement discipline is strong, but a one-screen signal metaphor obscures a browseable collection of dozens.
options.kept: Illustration scale remains stable while surrounding information recomposes responsively.
options.risk: It reads as laboratory instrumentation before it reads as cocktails.

options.label: The Liquid Shader Portal
options.thesis: Each cocktail opens as a living field of its own accent color behind a floating glass mark.
options.viewport: A single immersive cocktail dominates the screen while thin edge navigation moves through the collection.
options.case: The route transition is memorable, but serial browsing and factual recipe reading become secondary.
options.kept: The chosen SVG should persist and transform across the index-to-detail route change.
options.risk: Atmosphere overwhelms the collection and creates unnecessary runtime weight.

options.label: The Tiled Cocktail Hall
options.lineage: azulejo station halls and framed narrative panels
options.thesis: The collection unfolds as illustrated cocktail panels snapped to a visible tile grid.
options.viewport: Framed glass illustrations form a sequential hall whose bays expand by whole tile units.
options.case: It offers strong modular growth, but a cobalt-dominant world fights the YAML accent colors that distinguish recipes.
options.kept: Responsive layouts recompose by complete modules, never awkward fractions.
options.risk: Ornament becomes louder than recipe identity and compromises the neutral collection system.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished editorial recipe index with conventional image cards and clean detail pages.
canonCard.viewport: A centered title introduces a tidy responsive card grid; each card opens a familiar two-column recipe page.
canonCard.risk: Clear and usable, but visually interchangeable with many premium recipe sites.
